text: Malaysia, goods and services tax (GST). Until 31 May 2018 GST was charged at the standard rate of 6%. The 6% GST was implemented in 2015. A receipt or tax invoice from this period normally shows GST at 6%.
note: Start date: the sources say 2015 only. The exact day is not in them, so valid_from is left open. The sentence about what a receipt normally shows is our reading of the rule, checked against the SROIE receipts. In SROIE, 480 of the 487 receipts dated up to May 2018 that print a rate print 6%.

text: Malaysia, GST zero rate. From 1 June 2018 the GST rate was adjusted from 6% to 0% across Malaysia, ahead of the move to the sales and service tax (SST). A receipt from June to August 2018 normally shows GST at 0%.
note: Start 1 June 2018 is in the ActivPayroll page. The end date 31 August 2018 is inferred from SST starting on 1 September 2018. ActivPayroll alone says 6% GST is deactivated from 1 August 2018, so receipts in August 2018 may differ. The sentence about what a receipt normally shows is our reading of the rule, checked against the SROIE receipts. In SROIE, 44 of the 47 receipts dated June to August 2018 that print a rate print 0%.

text: Malaysia, sales tax under the sales and service tax (SST), which replaces GST from 1 September 2018. Sales tax is charged at 5% or 10% depending on the goods, and at a specific amount for petroleum products.
note: Both pages were written before SST started (planned or expected wording). Rates may have changed later; this chunk is for receipts from 2018 to early 2019.

text: Malaysia, service tax under the sales and service tax (SST), in force from 1 September 2018. The service tax rate is fixed at 6%. A receipt after this date can show service tax at 6% instead of GST.
note: The sources say the rate is 6%; both were written before SST started. Which services are taxable is not covered here. The sentence about what a receipt normally shows is our reading of the rule, checked against the SROIE receipts.

text: Indonesia, restaurant tax (PB1, now part of the regional tax on certain goods and services, PBJT). It is a regional tax, not the national VAT (PPN). The maximum rate is 10% (Law 1 of 2022 on central and regional financial relations, Article 58). Each regional government sets its own rate, which can be lower than 10%.
note: Receipts in CORD carry no dates, so no validity period is set. The source describes the current law; older receipts were under Law 28 of 2009, whose details were not checked here.

text: Indonesia, how restaurant tax (PB1) is calculated: PB1 payable = total customer payment x PB1 rate. Example from the source: a bill of Rp 500,000 at a 10% rate gives Rp 50,000 of tax, and the customer pays Rp 550,000 in total. The tax is an amount of money printed on the receipt, not the percentage.
note: The source does not say whether a service charge is part of the base; do not infer that.
